learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.

Students should know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their area of study.

Students should be able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of formulating judgments based on information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Students should know how to communicate their conclusions and the ultimate knowledge and reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Students should possess the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a way that will largely be self-directed or autonomous.

Have adequate knowledge of the scientific and technological aspects of: mathematical, analytical and numerical methods in engineering, electrical engineering, energy engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, continuum mechanics, industrial electronics, automation, manufacturing, materials, quantitative management methods, industrial computing, urban planning and infrastructure.
Plan, calculate and design products, processes, facilities and plants.
Carry out research, development and innovation in products, processes and methods.
Carry out strategic planning and apply it to construction, production, quality and environmental management systems.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Engineer.
Knowledge and ability for the analysis and design of electrical energy generation, transport and distribution systems.
Knowledge and skills for the design and analysis of thermal machines and engines, hydraulic machines and industrial heating and cooling installations.
Knowledge and skills that allow understanding, analyzing, exploiting and managing the different energy sources.
Know the lines of energy policy and advanced technologies for thermoelectric generation with minimum pollutant emissions.
Apply, evaluate and analyze clean thermoelectric generation technologies under different technical possibilities according to the types of applications.
Select and apply pollutant emission reduction technologies in combustion gases.

syllabus_topics: Energy planning for reducing pollutant emissions
Basic circuits in a thermal power plant
Clean technologies. SC and USC thermal power plants
Clean technologies. Integrated Gasification Combined Cycle
Sources of pollutant emissions in thermoelectric generation
Analysis of the combustion process: Combustion balance of a fuel
Analysis of the combustion process: Determination of boiler efficiency in a thermal power plant
Analysis of the combustion process: Emission balance in a thermal power plant
Analysis of a combined cycle thermal power plant
Analysis of a biomass thermal power plant
Study of contents of each thematic unit and practical cases
Individual preparation of an assigned work
teaching_methods: Non-contact work (Virtual Campus activities, autonomous work)

assessment_methods.method: Practical evaluation tests (laboratory and computer classroom practices)

assessment_rules: For ordinary and extraordinary calls, the final grade is calculated as NF = N*0.6 + PC*0.10 + PL*0.3, where N is the exam grade, PC is class participation, and PL is practical tests. Incorrect answers on the exam are penalized using the formula N = ((A - Err/(d-1))/n)*10. For differentiated evaluation, the final grade is NF = N*0.7 + PL*0.3, where N is the final theory exam and PL is the final practical exam. No minimum grade is required for any individual evaluable component.
